name: R
summary: Dynamically typed, lazily evaluated, vector-oriented language and environment for statistical computing and graphics; an open-source dialect of S with Scheme-style lexical scoping, first-class environments and several object systems (S3, S4, reference classes).

level_notes.0: GNU R (developed in Subversion, mirrored at wch/r-source) is the reference implementation and the de-facto definition. Alternative implementations: FastR (GraalVM), Renjin (JVM), pqR, Ř/RIR (research JIT), webR (GNU R on WebAssembly).
level_notes.1: No standard or formal specification. The 'R Language Definition' manual is officially still a draft; together with R Internals, Writing R Extensions and the per-function help pages it is the primary description. There is no numbered proposal process: R Core decides, with discussion on R-devel and Bugzilla. The Core R semantics in Morandat et al. (ECOOP 2012) is the main formalisation.
level_notes.2: 'An Introduction to R' is the official tutorial; Advanced R is the standard deep treatment of the language itself.
